summary.text:
South Cambridgeshire's 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy is a well-laid-out annual paper — the Medium Term Forecast (Annex C), Liability Benchmark (Annex D) and Actual Portfolio (Annex B) all rebuild against each other and the balance-sheet identity ties to £0.0m at both 31.3.2025 and 31.3.2026. The distinctive feature is the Ermine Street Housing loan: £119.2m of the £172.7m 'treasury investments' headline at 31 December 2025 sits with the Council's own wholly owned housing company against a £120m approved ceiling (99.3% utilised). Add in the £14.3m to South Cambs Investment Partnership and £2.4m to Cambridge Leisure and £135.9m of the £172.7m is related-entity lending; genuinely external liquid treasury is £37.1m.

The HRA side is the operational hook. §8.2 flags £129m of PWLB HRA New Build drawing forming part of the £344.123m long-term book projected for year-end, and §8.5 records the 0.60% preferential HRA discount extended to 31 March 2027. On today's 50-year curve the HRA rate is 5.87% against Certainty 6.27% — 40 basis points, or about £0.52m per year on a fully drawn £129m book while the enhanced rate lasts.

Internal borrowing runs £124.2m at 31.3.2026 rising slowly to £135.0m at 31.3.2029 — it does not fall away — and Annex D's Liability Benchmark sits about £18m above planned external borrowing in each of the four forecast years. The MRP policy has been rewritten to remove the prior 'receipts will repay the debt' exemption at §9.7 and to update the wholly-owned company loans clause (Annex E(8)) for the April 2024 statutory guidance. MUFG's 22 December 2025 forecast expects Bank Rate to reach 3.25% by Q4 2026; on 14 August the curve sits about half a point higher across all tenors than the year-end 2025 reference.

Loan-book reconciliation via price_book failed — the Start dates on our file are unreliable at point-in-time — so the email opens on the Ermine Street composition rather than a headline tie. Our file at 16.8.2026 holds 49 loans totalling £266.7m against their Annex B £259.1m at 31.12.2025, broadly consistent across 8 months of new drawing.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts ahead of the Treasury Management Strategy going to Council on 24 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The strategy is clearly laid out and the annexes rebuild against each other, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

Your Annex B shows £172.7m of treasury investments, and £119.2m of that is the Ermine Street Housing loan against a £120m approved limit — 99.3% utilised. Add the £14.3m to South Cambs Investment Partnership and the £2.4m to Cambridge Leisure and Ice Centre and £135.9m of the £172.7m is loans to related entities. Genuinely external liquid treasury — banks, DMADF and other local authorities, money market funds — is £37.1m. Nothing about that is wrong; a housing company you own funding a policy you set is a legitimate use of the balance sheet. But of the councils we've read this is a more concentrated shape than most, and it is a piece of information that gets lost when the £172.7m appears as a single line.

The HRA side has an operational angle worth surfacing. §8.5 records the PWLB HRA discount at 0.60% below Standard, extended to 31 March 2027, and §8.2 flags £129m of PWLB HRA New Build drawing forming part of the £344.123m long-term book projected for year-end. On today's curve — 14 August, notice 314/26 PM — 50-year Certainty is 6.27% and 50-year HRA is 5.87%, a 40 basis point differential. On a £129m book fully drawn at 50 years that is about £0.52m a year in perpetuity while the enhanced rate lasts. Whether any of the £129m fits inside the discount window is a New Build cash flow question, not a market question — but the window closes on a stated date and the arithmetic is knowable.

One market note against your MUFG forecast, dated 22 December 2025. It starts Mar-26 with 5-year Certainty at 4.60%, 25-year at 5.80% and 50-year at 5.60%, drifting down through 2028. The 14 August fixings are 5-year 5.34%, 25-year 6.46% and 50-year 6.27% — about half a point higher across the curve than the year-end 2025 reference. Bank Rate is still 3.75% and MUFG's Q2 2026 cut has not yet happened. That doesn't invalidate the forecast; it dates the reference point, and members may find it useful to see how the curve has moved between the strategy being drafted and the meeting.

We track PWLB drawings and rates daily at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — July's PWLB lending was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%. Every council's book is priced against the DMO's repayment curve at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

On training, four fit South Cambridgeshire. HRA treasury & self-financing speaks to the New Build programme's timing against the 0.60% window. MRP — policy options and revenue impact maps to your rewritten Annex E(8) on wholly-owned company loans. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice lines up with the £124m–£135m internal borrowing carry across your forecast. And Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets covers the £58m of LA short-term already in your book. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Sources: Treasury Management Strategy, Council, 24 February 2026 (docs 142409 covering and 142410 Appendix A); MUFG Corporate Markets economic and interest rate forecast as at 22 December 2025 (Annex A of Appendix A).
